subject: Dedicated reservation options and activation sprint for Anthemic AI
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@anthemic.ai>

Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:14:22 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — rough ask and timing

Hi Marissa / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Anthemic is ready to move from pilots to committed capacity and we want to model a conservative onboarding path so we don't get blocked during our fall product launch. Attached is a short usage sheet showing expected RPS and token volumes. High-level ask:

- We need a committed reservation that starts small but guarantees a minimum lane for our inference-critical traffic (low-latency chat and re-ranking).
- Target: 30 min GPUs day-1, scale to ~220 active GPUs by month 9.
- Prefer ~2 staged ramps (Q3 warm, Q4 full activation) with a brief canary before each stage.
- Interested in warm-start credits and an activation runway (we'd be open to committing earlier for a softened bill in month 1).

Can you send the reservation options, minimal guaranteed floor, and a recommended ramp schedule? Also include any typical SLAs and how fallbacks/overflow would work if we suddenly need burst capacity.

Emily
VP Product, Anthemic AI
ops@anthemic.ai

Attachment: Anthemic_Dedicated_Request.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@anthemic.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 11:02:08 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — rough ask and timing

Emily — thanks for the clear brief and the sheet. Attaching an initial proposal (v1) and a ramp workbook that maps your timeline to three reservation variants. TL;DR recommendations below, full details in the PDF:

1) Starter Floor (conservative)
- Minimum guaranteed: 32 GPUs (x86 A100-equivalent lanes)
- Burst pool: access to shared hosted burst capacity up to +20% of base during business hours (best-effort)
- Activation: 4-week canary (2 GPUs reserved for canary), full 32-GPU activation month 2
- Pricing: 12-month commit with month-1 warm-start credit = 25% credit on month 1 invoice

2) Stepped Ramp (recommended for your 2-stage plan)
- Phase 1 (Q3 warm): commit 64 GPUs, with ability to step to 128 after 60 days
- Phase 2 (Q4 full): ramp to 192–224 GPUs across months 5–9 depending on usage triggers
- Minimum guarantee during ramp: 64 GPUs until step trigger executed
- Autoscaling policy: dedicated lane autoscale + soft overflow to compatible quantized variants on hosted fleet to preserve latency SLOs

3) Performance-First (aggressive)
- Minimum guaranteed: 128 GPUs + hot-standby pool of 16 GPUs for immediate burst
- Onboarding credits and dedicated engineering onboarding window (2 weeks)

Notes on SLAs / fallbacks:
- Uptime SLA (dedicated): 99.9% per month (credits applied for breaches)
- Latency SLO: 95th pct tokens latency target included per model in the proposal; fallback routing to a compatible variant occurs automatically if dedicated lane capacity is exhausted (we throttle to preserve tail latency).
- KV/prefix cache preservation: suggest a 48–72 hour prewarm window before each major step to minimize cold-start rate.

Next steps: if the Stepped Ramp looks right, I'll loop in Solutions Eng for a one-hour sizing workshop (we'll run a short simulation with your provided RPS). I attached: Anthemic_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.pdf and activation_ramp_schedule.xlsx.

—Marissa
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attachment: Anthemic_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.pdf (13 pages)
Attachment: activation_ramp_schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet, 18KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 15:22:54 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — rough ask and timing

Emily — quick technical notes to add on the proposal. Marissa captured the commercial options; below are operational pieces we'll need to align on before sign: 

- Canary plan: recommend a 10-day canary (subset of traffic) using a dedicated canary pool (2–4 GPUs) and real traffic replay. We'll collect latency/95th percentiles and tail token CPU usage.
- Warm-start: for your models we suggest an initial KV prefill pass and running synthetic prefix sweeps during the 72-hour prewarm window; this reduces cold-token spikes once ramp occurs. We can include 8 hours of hands-on prewarm ops as part of onboarding.
- Model variants: if you plan to use quantized variants for cost during burst, we should lock the model family and evaluation prompts now so Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles without risking quality regressions.
- Monitoring hooks: include token-level cost dashboards and an alert for token-quality regressions tied to your eval set.

Operationally: if you sign the 12-month stepped ramp, we typically lock the phase triggers by porting the activation schedule to our internal rollout controller and setting conservative thresholds for the first two ramp steps. That gives you predictable burn-rate and an escape window if traffic doesn't materialize.

Happy to run through the activation_ramp_schedule spreadsheet in a 30-min sync. Are you free Wed (6/3) 11am PT?

—Ben
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
